experiment: [γ-32P]ATP CheA autophosphorylation time course (gel/phosphorimager), first-order fit, CheA + CheW only
buffer: TKEDM: 50 mM KCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5 mM Tris
construct_or_mutation: E. coli CheA (full-length not explicitly specified), CheA monomer 1 µM, CheW 1 µM
other_conditions: Complex formed 1 h at 25 °C before ATP; CheA standard normalised at 30 s; related structures: none. Supplied P1 entry vs whole-protein kinetic assay.
dynamics_type: slow inactive/active exchange of kinase (inferred from kinetics)
timescale: k1 = 1.18 ± 0.05 min –1; k1A0 = 1.2 CheA-P min –1 (first-order fit, Pt = A0(1 – e–k1t))
population: A0 = 0.99 ± 0.01 (CheA-P relative to free CheA standard)
author_claim: Free CheA is largely inactive, with a small active fraction that exchanges slowly with the inactive form on the experimental time scale, so autophosphorylation saturates quickly but at a low level.
locator: Table 2; conditions: Methods (CheA Autophosphorylation Assays), Figure 8 legend
caveat_note: Inactive/active CheA exchange is inferred from the plateau and rate of a bulk phosphorylation assay, not observed directly. No structural or residue-level information for the P1 domain. The measured k1 is a phosphorylation rate constant, not a measured exchange rate, and it is the fitted autophosphorylation rate for CheA–CheW (the paper notes it is similar to a previous value for CheA alone).

experiment: [γ-32P]ATP CheA autophosphorylation time course, first-order fit, CheA + CheW + TarSC 4Q
buffer: TKEDM: 50 mM KCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5 mM Tris
ligand_or_partner: CheW; TarSC 4Q (single-chain Tar KCM dimer, not trimerised); [γ-32P]ATP
construct_or_mutation: E. coli CheA (full-length not explicitly specified); TarSC 4Q (Tar KCM 257–521 single-chain dimer, E302Q/E491Q-type 4Q adaptation mutations)
other_conditions: 1:1:3 CheA monomer:CheW:MCP dimer; TarSC 3 µM, CheA 1 µM; complexed 1 h at 25 °C; related structures: none. MALS-SEC showed little complex formation of TarSC with CheA–CheW.
dynamics_type: slow inactive-to-active conversion of kinase (inferred from kinetics)
timescale: k1 = 0.09 ± 0.02 min –1; k1A0 = 0.7 CheA-P min –1 (first-order fit)
population: A0 = 8 ± 1 (CheA-P relative to free CheA standard)
author_claim: Tar variants raise the fraction of active CheA and facilitate slow conversion from an inactive to an active form.
locator: Table 2; conditions: Methods and Figure 8 legend
caveat_note: The inactive/active interconversion is an interpretation of the plateau size and slow k1; rate constants are dominated by plateau behaviour at long times. Biexponential fits could not be resolved. MALS-SEC suggests TarSC forms little complex, so the effect is not tied to a defined assembly.

experiment: [γ-32P]ATP CheA autophosphorylation time course, first-order fit, CheA + CheW + TarFO 4Q
buffer: TKEDM: 50 mM KCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5 mM Tris
construct_or_mutation: E. coli CheA (full-length not explicitly specified); TarFO 4Q 515 (construct 14, Tar KCM 257–521/257–515 single-chain dimer with C-terminal foldon, QQQQ)
other_conditions: 1:1:3 CheA monomer:CheW:MCP dimer; 1 µM each; complexed 1 h at 25 °C; related structures: none
dynamics_type: slow inactive-to-active conversion of kinase (inferred from kinetics)
timescale: k1 = 0.20 ± 0.06 min –1; k1A0 = 1.3 CheA-P min –1 (first-order fit)
population: A0 = 6.7 ± 0.9 (CheA-P relative to free CheA standard)
author_claim: Trimer-of-dimers mimetic TarFO 4Q increases the active CheA fraction and, with k1 largely representing the exchange rate, shows the greatest increase in CheY phosphotransfer.
locator: Table 2; conditions: Methods and Figure 8 legend
caveat_note: k1 is interpreted as an inactive-to-active exchange rate but this is an inference from bulk kinetics; an alternative is that receptors shift the fraction of competent kinase without measurable exchange. TarFO 4Q complexes are heterogeneous by MALS-SEC. The fit R2 is 0.95.

experiment: [γ-32P]ATP CheA autophosphorylation time course (up to 40 min), first-order fit, CheA + CheW + TarFO short
buffer: TKEDM: 50 mM KCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5 mM Tris
ligand_or_partner: CheW; TarFO short (PIR-only Tar 353–424 single-chain dimer with foldon); [γ-32P]ATP
construct_or_mutation: E. coli CheA (full-length not explicitly specified); TarFO short (construct 17, Tar 353–424 repeats, C-terminal foldon)
other_conditions: 1:1:3 CheA monomer:CheW:MCP dimer; 1 µM each; complexed 1 h at 25 °C; related structures: none
dynamics_type: slow inactive-to-active conversion of kinase (inferred from kinetics)
timescale: k1 = 0.073 ± 0.009 min –1; k1A0 = 1.3 CheA-P min –1 (first-order fit; a faster phase at <1.5 min suggested but not resolved in biexponential fits)

caveat_note: Inactive/active exchange is inferred from plateau and slow rate only. Low net CheY-P accumulation was attributed to rapid CheY-P hydrolysis (t1/2 ~ 30 s; k ~ 1.3 min –1) rather than limited phosphotransfer; an alternative two-stage activation was considered and not fully excluded.

experiment: Four-pulse DEER (PDS) of spin-labeled T. maritima CheA P3P4P5 Q545C-R1 with CheW and Tm14 (inhibitory) vs TarFO 4Q, 17.3 GHz
buffer: GFB: 50 mM Tris and 150 mM NaCl
ligand_or_partner: T. maritima CheW; Tm14 KCM (inhibitory) or E. coli TarFO 4Q (activating mimetic), 1:2:3 subunit ratio
construct_or_mutation: T. maritima CheA P3P4P5 (Δ289) Q545C-R1 (MTSSL); other proteins E. coli TarFO 4Q, T. maritima CheW and Tm14
other_conditions: 38 µM CheA; pull-down confirmed similar binding of Tm14 and TarFO 4Q to P3P4P5 and CheW; Tikhonov/MEM distance distributions; related structures: none; homolog (T. maritima) data, not E. coli CheA
dynamics_type: regulatory P5 domain conformational change (inhibited vs planar arrangement), flexibility
population: minor distance peak retained at the position seen with Tm14 (fraction not given)
author_claim: TarFO 4Q binding increases the P5–P5 spin separation by ~7 Å relative to Tm14 and broadens the distribution, consistent with a planar P5 arrangement as in membrane arrays, with some residual inhibited-like population.
anchor: complex spin-labeled at position 545 revealed that Tar FO  induces an ∼7 Å increase in the separation of the P5
locator: Results, Effects of TarFO on CheA Conformation; Figure 10A,B; conditions: Methods, Pulsed-Dipolar ESR Spectroscopy
caveat_note: This is T. maritima CheA P3P4P5 (residue numbering Q545 does not map onto the supplied E. coli P1 entry sequence, so residues_entry is empty), and the entry is the E. coli P1 domain; evidence is homolog and different domains. Broad distribution may reflect flexibility without interlocking rings or label conformers, and the authors note the broadness is not resolved into discrete states.
